questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias
questions.q: Which interstitium scheme opens the chapter on page 236?
opts: Interstitium is the air space within alveoli; alveolar interstitium splits into subpleural and lobar, vascular interstitium surrounds vessels, and axial interstitium connects lung to chest wall

Interstitium is connective tissue that holds the lungs together; alveolar interstitium splits into subpleural and segmental, vascular interstitium surrounds airways, and axial interstitium connects the two lungs

Interstitium is connective tissue that holds the lungs together; alveolar interstitium surrounds vessels, vascular interstitium splits into subpleural and lobar, and axial interstitium connects lung to chest wall

Interstitium is connective tissue that holds the lungs together; alveolar interstitium splits into subpleural and lobar, vascular interstitium surrounds vessels, and axial interstitium connects lung to chest wall

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

subpleural
vascular
axial

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias
questions.q: How is interstitial lung disease itself defined and driven on page 236?

It is 'Focal parenchymal lung fibrosis', a TGF-β > PDGF mediated parenchymal fibrosis, with TGF-β boxed as the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine
It is 'Diffuse parenchymal lung inflammation', a TGF-β > VEGF mediated parenchymal fibrosis, with VEGF boxed as the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine
It is 'Diffuse parenchymal lung fibrosis', a PDGF > TGF-β mediated parenchymal fibrosis, with PDGF boxed as the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine
questions.exp: The bullets read 'Diffuse parenchymal lung fibrosis' and 'TGF-β > PDGF mediated parenchymal fibrosis', and the side box states 'Note: TGF-β most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine.' The inequality runs TGF-β first. (Book p236)

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
Idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (m/c)

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

ARDS associated with diffuse alveolar damage; seen following bacterial sepsis; very poor prognosis
ARDS associated with diffuse alveolar damage; seen following COVID infection and viral infections; very poor prognosis
COP associated with diffuse alveolar damage; seen following COVID infection and viral infections; good prognosis

questions.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias

Acute interstitial pneumonia
Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

Rheumatoid arthritis, diffuse systemic sclerosis, inclusion body myositis, mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), Sjogren's syndrome and reactive arthritis
Rheumatoid arthritis, diffuse systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis (inflammatory muscle disease), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), Sjogren's syndrome and ankylosing spondylitis
Rheumatoid arthritis, limited systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis (inflammatory muscle disease), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), Sjogren's syndrome and ankylosing spondylitis

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

Vasculitis-related: eosinophilic granulomatosis polyangiitis (EGPA)/Churg-Strauss syndrome; inherited: neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis; drug-induced: bleomycin
Vasculitis-related: eosinophilic granulomatosis polyangiitis (EGPA)/Churg-Strauss syndrome; inherited: tuberous sclerosis only; drug-induced: bleomycin
Vasculitis-related: eosinophilic granulomatosis polyangiitis (EGPA)/Churg-Strauss syndrome; inherited: neurofibromatosis and cystic fibrosis; drug-induced: amiodarone

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

viral infection
asbestos
smoking

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

Idiopathic UIP/IPF is the most common; rheumatoid arthritis ILD occurs in males > females aged 50–70 years and is associated with smoking

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points
questions.q: Match each pattern with its page 237 'Important points' association — 1) NSIP 2) COP 3) LIP … A) Sjogren syndrome and HIV B) Young females with a subacute restrictive process, associated with drugs and connective tissue disease C) Most common pattern in inflammatory muscle disease (polymyositis and dermatomyositis)
questions.exp: NSIP is described as young females with a subacute restrictive process and associations of drug and connective tissue disease; COP is 'm/c in inflammatory muscle disease' branching to polymyositis and dermatomyositis; LIP lists Sjogren syndrome and HIV. (Book p237)

questions.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

Dry non-productive cough and dyspnea on exertion — together misdiagnosed as bronchitis

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

(Book p238)

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

questions.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR

questions.sec: PFT in Initial versus Advanced ILD, HRCT as Investigation of Choice and the UIP Pattern with Its Image Captions and New Antifibrotic Drugs

questions.sec: PFT in Initial versus Advanced ILD, HRCT as Investigation of Choice and the UIP Pattern with Its Image Captions and New Antifibrotic Drugs

units.title: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias
units.sec: Interstitium and Its Types, Lung Parenchyma, TGF-β/PDGF Fibrosis, ILD Classification and the Seven Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias
units.guide:
The interstitium (p236) is connective tissue holding the lungs together: alveolar (subpleural and lobar), vascular (surrounds vessels) and axial (connects lung to chest wall); lung parenchyma is alveoli plus alveolar and vascular interstitium.
ILD is 'diffuse parenchymal lung fibrosis', TGF-β > PDGF mediated, with TGF-β boxed as the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine, and classifies into idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (most common), autoimmune ILD, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, sarcoidosis and miscellaneous.
The seven idiopathic interstitial pneumonias run IPF/UIP (most common), NSIP (2nd), COP (3rd), RB-ILD and DIP bracketed as smoking-associated, acute interstitial pneumonia (ARDS with diffuse alveolar damage after COVID/viral infection, very poor prognosis), and LIP.

units.title: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points
units.sec: Autoimmune and Miscellaneous ILD (Occupational Lobes, Vasculitis, Inherited, Drug-Induced, LCH, LAM) with the UIP/NSIP/COP/LIP Important Points
units.guide:
Autoimmune ILD (p237) complicates rheumatoid arthritis, diffuse systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis, MCTD, Sjogren's syndrome and ankylosing spondylitis.
Miscellaneous ILD covers occupational disease (asbestosis lower lobe; silicosis, berylliosis and coal-worker's pneumoconiosis upper lobe), EGPA/Churg-Strauss vasculitis, inherited neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis, bleomycin, smoking-associated LCH (printed 'Langerhan's') and LAM.
Important points: idiopathic UIP/IPF is most common and RA-ILD affects smoking males of 50–70 years; NSIP affects young females as a subacute restrictive process linked to drugs and connective tissue disease; COP is most common in inflammatory muscle disease; LIP links to Sjogren syndrome and HIV; and the commonest pattern is UIP in RA but NSIP in other conditions.

units.title: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR
units.sec: Clinical Features of ILD: Cardinal Symptoms, the Crackles-and-Clubbing Table versus Bronchiectasis, Skin Signs, Pulmonary HTN Prognosis and CXR
units.guide:
ILD (p238) presents with two cardinal symptoms, dry non-productive cough and dyspnea on exertion, often misdiagnosed as bronchitis; fever with arthralgia suggests sarcoidosis, wheeze is specific to bronchiectasis/ABPA/hypersensitivity pneumonitis, pleuritic pain to asbestosis, and hemoptysis is rare.
Crackles in ILD are bilateral bibasal, fine 'velcro', end to early expiratory as printed, without cough/posture variation, against unilateral coarse early-to-mid inspiratory crackles in bronchiectasis; clubbing is present in ILD and absent in bronchiectasis except childhood cystic bronchiectasis, with cafe-au-lait spots, erythema nodosum and Raynaud's pointing to neurofibromatosis, sarcoidosis and scleroderma.
Hypoxia drives pulmonary vasoconstriction to pulmonary HTN, the most significant prognostic factor; OSAS (ruled out by sleep study) and ILD (by CT scan) present directly with pulmonary HTN, and the CXR shows bilateral bibasal subpleural reticular/reticulo-nodular infiltrates.

units.title: PFT in Initial versus Advanced ILD, HRCT as Investigation of Choice and the UIP Pattern with Its Image Captions and New Antifibrotic Drugs
units.sec: PFT in Initial versus Advanced ILD, HRCT as Investigation of Choice and the UIP Pattern with Its Image Captions and New Antifibrotic Drugs
units.guide:
Initially (p239) ILD is a type 1 respiratory failure with only diffusion impaired — impaired DLCO with normal FEV1 and FVC — advancing to type 3 failure with ventilation impaired, FVC falling sharply and FEV1/FVC normal or raised.
HRCT is the investigation of choice to determine pattern and prognosis: in UIP, linear shadows (intralobular septal thickening) and reticular shadows (net of linear opacities) are suggestive, while subpleural basal-predominant honeycombing (small polyhedral cystic spaces), loss of lung architecture and traction bronchiectasis complete the set bracketed specific for UIP, and nodules with ground glass opacification are absent.
The six scans are captioned honeycombing, traction bronchiectasis, reticular shadows and linear shadows, and the new UIP-ILD drugs are pirfenidone (anti-TGF) and nintedanib (anti-FDGF as printed, anti-VEGF, anti-PDGFR).

units.title: NSIP Pattern and Its Treatment, Drugs Causing ILD, COP/BOOP with Halo Signs, and Cysts on HRCT (LAM, LCH, LIP)
units.sec: NSIP Pattern and Its Treatment, Drugs Causing ILD, COP/BOOP with Halo Signs, and Cysts on HRCT (LAM, LCH, LIP)
units.guide:
NSIP (p240) shows bilateral postero-basal ground glass without parenchymal destruction, honeycombing or cystic spaces and a prognosis better than UIP; MMF is printed best, ahead of steroids and azathioprine.
Ten drugs cause NSIP-pattern ILD — amiodarone, bleomycin, busulfan, bromocriptine, nitrofurantoin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, anti-TNF, carmustine and mitomycin — with cyclophosphamide and methotrexate braced to hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
COP/BOOP affects elderly males (>60–70 years as printed) with Masson's buds, a pneumonia-like presentation and polymyositis/dermatomyositis associations; its restrictive type responds to steroids while the constrictive obstructive type does not, the reverse-halo sign (GGO inside consolidation) contrasts with the halo sign of invasive aspergillosis, and HRCT cysts split into LAM (young females, tuberous sclerosis/angiomyolipoma, pneumothorax and chylous effusion, everolimus), LCH (young male, upper lobe fibrosis, CD1a and Birbeck granules positive, smoking, lytic lesions, diabetes insipidus) and LIP (Sjogren's, HIV).

units.title: HRCT Finding–Disease Table, Nodular Shadows and Tree-in-Bud Notes with the Mosaic Attenuation and Lower-Lobe Infiltrate Captions
units.sec: HRCT Finding–Disease Table, Nodular Shadows and Tree-in-Bud Notes with the Mosaic Attenuation and Lower-Lobe Infiltrate Captions
units.guide:
The HRCT table (p241) maps reticular/linear shadows, traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing to UIP; nodular shadows to LCH/LAM; ground glass to NSIP; consolidations to COP; mosaic attenuation/air trapping to HP; and cysts to LCH/LAM/LIP.
Nodular shadows are a non-specific feature caused by LAM, LCH, LIP and RB-ILD, and tree-in-bud reflects endobronchial obstruction associated with infections.
The page's scans are captioned 'HRCT findings in ILD: Nodular shadows', 'mosaic attenuation in ILD (Hypersensitivity pneumonitis)' and 'Ill-defined infiltrates in lower lobe'.

units.title: Conditions with Upper-Lobe ILD, the LL Reticular Caption in IPF, and Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (PAP)
units.sec: Conditions with Upper-Lobe ILD, the LL Reticular Caption in IPF, and Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (PAP)
units.guide:
Upper-lobe ILD (p242) groups the occupational trio silicosis, berylliosis and coal-worker's pneumoconiosis, the CTD pair sarcoidosis and ankylosing spondylitis as printed, and ABPA, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, TB with upper-lobe fibrosis and LCH; the illustrating film is nonetheless captioned 'LL reticular shadows in IPF'.
PAP affects 30–50-year males as printed without a unit: congenital disease from SP-B mutation, and acquired most-common disease from anti-GM-CSF antibodies reducing surfactant clearance.
Its clinical feature is chunky gelatinous PAS-positive sputum, the X-ray shows a batwing appearance with silicosis as differential, and treatment is whole lung lavage.
